angle: Movement translation, DL (clearest of five groups screened): each rusher's tracked Combine 40 start laid over his own random NFL pass-rush starts. Curve similarity (carry-over and four other scores) does not explain pressure beyond pick; agreement between the two speed signals (official 40 time x NFL first step) does, as a held-out shortlist scored against a base rate.
metric_name: Speed that translates (the 'Both' call): NFL first step (mean speed 0.3-0.5 s after first movement on ~20 random sampled pass rushes, alignment-adjusted, after weight and EDGE share) in the top third AND official 40 time in the top half, with each class's cut-offs set on the other two classes; rule hashed in frozen_rule.json
headline_number: Held-out shortlist: 8 of 10 rushers beat the no-tracking pressure forecast vs 16 of 59 others (base 35%), gap 53 pts [27, 75], within-class shuffle p 0.009; +5.0 pressures/season over forecast vs -1.4. Holds with a ridge forecast (8/10 vs 14/59) and with all sampled snaps removed from the outcome (7/10 vs 16/59). Translation itself is null: rho 0.07 after weight/role (n=67).
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_12/cand_3 (8.24), applying the round-12 judges' top_changes. (1) The positive use now leads: a pro-personnel shortlist ('speed that translates') whose cut-offs are set on the other two classes, scored by hit rate against the base rate and all other rushers, with a within-class label shuffle, a player bootstrap of the gap and drop-one. (2) Outcome checks that do not hinge on one player or on leakage: ridge forecast, a forecast that already knows the 40 time and NGS get-off, an outcome with every sampled snap removed, quick pressures and sacks; weaker results are reported plainly. (3) New Fig 3 (shortlist map against held-out cut-offs + hit-rate panel with base-rate ticks); old Fig 3 carry-over map and Fig 5 robustness are cut and their numbers moved to the Appendix. (4) Jargon (quasi-binomial, pooling, best-of-windows, calibration slopes, ridge penalty) moved to the Appendix; sample-flow table removed; 4-row ledger kept. (5) Board: Jordan Burch added as the shortlist miss; Maason Smith framed as the case where the rule disagrees with the tape, with a coaching fix. (6) Word count by wc -w is 1,909 (check.py 1,797); 4 figures + 2 tables.
open_risks: The two-signal form was chosen in round 12 after seeing all three classes; only the cut-offs are held out, so this is not a blind test (2026 is the first true one)
The shortlist has only 10 rushers, 9 from 2023-24; the single 2025 member (Jordan Burch) missed
Against a forecast that already knows the 40 time and NGS get-off the shortlist edge shrinks (6/10 vs 15/59, p ~0.08), and on quick pressures and sacks it is not significant
The angle's literal question (does curve similarity translate?) is still a null; the tracking contribution is the NFL first step, the Combine contribution is the stopwatch
Board actions are football judgement, not model output; no blockers, ball or scheme in the sampled tape
